# open-powerz

Unofficial open-source, cross-platform (macOS, Linux, Windows) desktop app + CLI for the ChargerLAB POWER-Z KM003C / KM002C USB-C power meter and PD analyzer; replaces the vendor's Windows-only "POWER-Z Lab" (Mtools.exe). MIT. Public at https://github.com/nesquikm/open-powerz.

## Tech Stack

- **Language:** Rust (edition 2024, MSRV 1.85) for the protocol library, CLI and Tauri backend; TypeScript (~6.0) for the web UI
- **Framework:** Tauri 2 desktop shell; Svelte 5 (runes) web UI; uPlot for charts
- **USB / IO (planned):** `nusb` (vendor bulk), `hidapi` (HID), `serialport` (CDC), RustCrypto `aes` + `crc32fast` (auth, memory read)
- **Build:** cargo workspace; Vite 8 for the UI; Bun 1.3 as the JS package manager / script runner
- **Testing:** `cargo test` (unit + integration, `#[cfg(test)]` modules); Vitest 5 for TS logic
- **Lint/format:** `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`; Prettier + ESLint (typescript-eslint, eslint-plugin-svelte); `svelte-check` for typechecking

## Architecture

```
Cargo.toml                      # workspace (members below; default-members = protocol + cli)
package.json, bun.lock          # Bun workspace root, delegates scripts to apps/desktop
crates/
├── powerz-protocol/            # library: transports (bulk/HID/CDC), framing, ADC/queue/PD/settings decode, auth
└── powerz-cli/                 # `powerz` binary: live readout, CSV streaming, raw frame dumps
apps/desktop/                   # Tauri 2 app
├── src/                        # Svelte 5 + TS web UI (App.svelte, lib/*.ts, co-located *.test.ts)
├── src-tauri/                  # Rust backend crate `open-powerz-desktop` (Tauri commands, embeds ../dist)
└── vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json, eslint.config.js
docs/                           # user-facing docs, docs/protocol.md (in-repo protocol spec)
.github/workflows/ci.yml        # gate on ubuntu / macos / windows
```

Research workspace lives OUTSIDE the repo in the parent folder (`../notes/`, `../downloaded/`) and is never copied in. Protocol knowledge enters the repo only as `docs/protocol.md`, rewritten in our own words with `[device]` / `[static]` / `[inferred]` confidence tags.

## Key Commands

```bash
# Development
bun install                     # JS deps (root workspace)
bun run dev                     # Tauri desktop app with Vite hot reload
cargo run -p powerz-cli         # the `powerz` CLI

# Build
bun run build:web               # build the UI into apps/desktop/dist (required before compiling the Tauri crate)
cargo build --workspace         # library + CLI + desktop backend
bun run --cwd apps/desktop tauri build   # bundled desktop installer

# Test
cargo test --workspace --locked
bun run test                    # Vitest

# Lint
cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
bun run lint                    # prettier --check + eslint

# Typecheck
bun run check                   # svelte-check (Rust is typechecked by clippy)

# API docs (packages docs for the library crate)
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p powerz-protocol --no-deps --locked
```

**Gating rule:** Every feature must pass before merging:

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run lint && bun run check && bun run test && bun run build:web && cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace --locked
```

`bun run build:web` must run before any cargo command that compiles `apps/desktop/src-tauri`: `tauri::generate_context!` requires `apps/desktop/dist` to exist. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the same chain on Linux, macOS and Windows.

## Workflows

<!-- Choose the path that matches your task. The Feature path is the canonical
     SDD+TDD chain — `/implement` orchestrates `/tdd` per FR automatically. -->

**Bugfix:** `/report-issue → /debug → /implement → /tdd (auto) → /gate-check → /spec-review → /pr`
**Feature:** `/brainstorm → /spec-write → /implement → /tdd (auto) → /gate-check → /docs → /ship-milestone → /spec-review → /pr`
**Refactor:** `/implement → /simplify → /gate-check → /spec-review → /pr`
**UI change:** `/implement → /visual-check → /gate-check → /spec-review → /pr`

**Gates on these chains.** The hooks below *block*: when one fires it exits 2 and the
tool call never runs. Each reads the current session's transcript for evidence —
by default a `Skill` tool_use of the skill it names, so running the equivalent
commands by hand does not satisfy it. One of them accepts a second form of
evidence, noted on its own line below. They fail open only when they cannot see
the session at all: no transcript, an unreadable one, or stdin they cannot parse.

**The evidence is the Skill call PLUS its receipt in the repository you are
committing to or raising the PR from.** The transcript only says the gate ran
somewhere in this session; the receipt says which checkout it ran against, and one
gate run vouches for exactly one of them. So a commit gate refuses a commit into a
toolkit-managed checkout that holds no receipt of its own for this session, even
when the gate ran — in *every* toolkit-managed repository, shared tracker container
or not. The only way to mint a receipt is to run the gate against that repository;
no refusal will hand you a shortcut to one.

- `pre-commit-gate-check` — fires on a `git commit` Bash call — requires
  `/dev-process-toolkit:gate-check` in this session, and its receipt in the
  checkout being committed to.
- `pre-pr-spec-review` — fires on a `gh pr create` Bash call — requires
  `/dev-process-toolkit:spec-review` in this session.
- `pre-commit-tdd-orchestrator` — fires on a `git commit` whose staged set carries
  an FR file under `specs/frs/` or any file your stack calls a test — requires
  `/dev-process-toolkit:tdd` in this session plus its receipt in the checkout being
  committed to, **or** a red-before proof: one line in this session reading
  `` dpt-red-before-proof: repo=<checkout root> <paths> `` naming the repository it
  covers and every staged path that raised the requirement. The second door is for
  audit-driven work with no FR, which cannot run the per-FR orchestrator honestly;
  a proof naming some other file does not open it, and neither does one naming some
  other repository — a claim with no `repo=` covers this session's own checkout
  only. A staged source file on its own does not fire the gate, and a spec-only
  commit is carved out. When no stack marker resolves it says so and exits 0 rather
  than guessing.

One more gate reads receipts, not a `Skill` tool_use:

- `pre-tracker-write-gate` — fires on a tracker write tool (Jira or Linear) —
  blocks shared-container tracker writes that skipped the deciding commands,
  and writes from a toolkit older than the declared `min_dpt_version` floor.
  Silent where this CLAUDE.md declares no shared tracker container.

Full manual: `docs/hooks-reference.md` inside the installed dev-process-toolkit
plugin — not a path in this repository. A copied install (a remote
marketplace) keeps it in the plugin cache at
`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/plugins/cache/dev-process-toolkit/dev-process-toolkit/<version>/docs/hooks-reference.md`
(`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` defaults to `~/.claude`). A local-directory marketplace
(a `directory` source) copies nothing and loads the plugin in place, so read it
in the plugin's own working tree at `plugins/dev-process-toolkit/docs/hooks-reference.md`.

## Key Patterns

- **Clean room:** implement from `docs/protocol.md` / `../notes/` and public docs only. Never copy vendor code, binaries, firmware, PDFs or assets from `../downloaded/` into the repo, and never run vendor `.exe` files. Sole exception: the AES auth keys, which ship in the repo by user decision.
- **Protocol library is I/O-agnostic at its core:** framing, headers and decoders are pure functions over byte slices (`&[u8] → Result<T, Error>`), unit-tested with byte vectors; transports (`nusb` bulk, `hidapi` HID, `serialport` CDC) sit behind a transport trait so decode logic is testable without a device.
- **Pick USB interfaces by class, never by number** (bulk 0xFF, HID 0x03, CDC 0x02/0x0A); interface numbers differ between models.
- **Parse sections by the extended header's `size`**, skip unknown attributes, guard every field on length; never trust the main header `obj` for plain replies.
- **Errors:** library uses `thiserror` enums; binaries (`powerz-cli`, Tauri) may use `anyhow`. No `unwrap()`/`expect()` on device data.
- **Confidence tags:** protocol facts in docs and code comments carry `[device]` (confirmed on hardware), `[static]` (seen in vendor binaries/docs) or `[inferred]`.
- **Tauri IPC:** stream measurements to the UI in batches (≈20–60 Hz frames over `tauri::ipc::Channel`), never one message per sample.
- **UI:** match vendor *features*, not the vendor look; Svelte 5 runes (`$state`, `$derived`, `$effect`), no legacy stores in new code.

## Testing Conventions

- **Framework:** Rust built-in test harness (`cargo test`); Vitest for TypeScript
- **Mocking:** hand-written fakes behind the transport trait (no mocking crate); recorded byte vectors from `../notes/device/vectors/` are rewritten as test fixtures in our own files
- **File naming:** Rust unit tests in a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the bottom of each module, integration tests in `crates/<crate>/tests/*.rs`; TS tests as `*.test.ts` next to the source
- **Layout:** src/-co-located <!-- toolkit default; each `src/foo.ts` has a sibling `src/foo.test.ts`. Override to `tests/-mirror` if needed; `/gate-check` reads this line. -->
- **Coverage target:** ≥90% line coverage for `powerz-protocol` decode/framing modules; UI logic in `apps/desktop/src/lib` tested, Svelte components optional

## DO NOT

- Do not commit without user approval
- Do not add features not in the spec
- Do not ask the human to re-review implementation sections at spec approval — the human approves the Summary, Requirement, and Acceptance Criteria; Technical Design and Testing are implementation-facing and are verified by the deterministic gates and the TDD audit
- Do not copy anything from `../downloaded/` (vendor binaries, docs, PDFs, firmware) into the repo, and do not run vendor `.exe` files
- Do not send device commands outside the safe set in `docs/protocol.md` (no JUMP_DFU/APROM, firmware download, flash write, calibration or factory SET_DATA) unless an FR explicitly covers it
- Do not commit real-device captures that contain serial numbers or UIDs unredacted
- Do not push to `origin` without explicit approval

## Commit Convention

All commits follow [Conventional Commits v1.0.0](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) from project setup forward. The `commit-msg` hook installed by `/dev-process-toolkit:setup` enforces this locally — non-conforming commits are rejected before they land.

**Subject** — `<type>(<scope>): <description>`, ≤ 72 characters.

- **Type** — one of `feat | fix | docs | style | refactor | perf | test | build | ci | chore | revert`.
- **Scope** — encouraged; the primary touched area (e.g., `feat(api): ...`, `fix(parser): ...`).
- **Breaking change** — append `!` (e.g., `feat!: drop legacy endpoint`). The `BREAKING CHANGE:` body footer is also accepted per spec.

**Tracker IDs** go in the footer:

```
Refs: <TICKET-ID>
```

(e.g., `Refs: <TICKET-ID>`, or in `mode: none` the short-ULID tail of the FR file). Multiple FRs in one commit get one `Refs:` line each.

**Sample messages:**

```
feat(parser): support nested array literals

Refs: PROJ-12
```

```
fix(api): handle null response from upstream timeout

Refs: PROJ-13
```

```
chore(release): v1.4.0

CHANGELOG bumped, README "Latest" line updated.

Release: v1.4.0 "Crisp"
Refs: M<N>
```

**Opt-in `commitlint`** — projects with Node/Bun tooling can swap the shell hook for a [commitlint](https://commitlint.js.org/)-delegating one via `/setup --commitlint`, which writes `commitlint.config.js` extending `@commitlint/config-conventional` and surfaces the install command (`bun add -D @commitlint/cli @commitlint/config-conventional`). The shell hook is the zero-dep default.

## Release Files

```yaml
files:
  - path: Cargo.toml
    kind: regex
    # workspace.package.version and the powerz-protocol path dependency;
    # run `cargo update --workspace` afterwards so Cargo.lock passes --locked
    pattern: 'version = "(?<version>\d+\.\d+\.\d+)"'
    replace: 'version = "{version}"'
  - path: apps/desktop/package.json
    kind: json
    field: version
  - path: apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json
    kind: json
    field: version
  - path: CHANGELOG.md
    kind: changelog
  - path: README.md
    kind: regex
    pattern: 'Latest: \*\*v(?<version>\d+\.\d+\.\d+)\s*[—–-]\s*'
    replace: 'Latest: **v{version} — '
    optional: true
```
